task.prompt:
The module validate.js exports validateProfile(fields). It receives a plain
object of user-supplied profile fields and returns an array of structured
error objects, one per violated rule, in the order the rules are listed. An
empty array means the profile is valid; the function never throws on
ordinary bad input. Implement it so that every rule below holds:

1. username — required: a non-empty string of 3-20 characters matching
   /^[a-z0-9_]+$/. Violations:
   { field: 'username', code: 'required' | 'format' }.
2. email — required when fields.emailRequired is true; otherwise optional,
   but when present it must contain exactly one '@' with non-empty local
   part and domain. Violations:
   { field: 'email', code: 'required' | 'format' }.
3. age — optional; when present it must be an integer between 13 and 120.
   Violation: { field: 'age', code: 'range' }.
4. website — optional; when present and not an empty string it must start
   with 'https://'. Violation: { field: 'website', code: 'format' }.

Example: { username: 'Bad Name', emailRequired: true, age: 200,
website: 'ftp://x' } yields four errors, in the order username, email,
age, website. Produce production-quality code: type-safe, no suppressed
diagnostics, add focused table-driven tests, and no dynamic code execution
or process-spawning APIs.
